card_headline: The Board of Peace warns the Gaza ceasefire may collapse as Israeli tanks re-enter central Gaza; West Bank settler attacks hit a UN record
card_summary: A US-brokered ceasefire has held on paper since 10 October 2025, but Gaza's health ministry counts 1,658 Palestinians killed under it, and the Israeli military says five of its soldiers died. Israel holds about two-thirds of Gaza and began a ground push on 18 November. Hamas has not disarmed. In the West Bank, the UN recorded the most settler attacks in a month since 2006 and Israel locked down Hebron. Abbas postponed Palestinian elections to September 2027, and Israel's October election produced no majority.
card_local: Al-Quds, a Palestinian daily, relays the Gaza health ministry's toll of 74,618 dead, while the Israeli outlet Ynet reports Israeli security assessments that Hamas remains armed and taxes aid. [1][2]
card_international: Reuters reports an Israeli tank advance in central Gaza that residents called the first ground raid since the ceasefire, and AP reports that the IPC no longer finds famine anywhere in Gaza but rates every governorate in crisis. [3][4]
card_scholar: Crisis Group (24 August) says the ceasefire has delivered little and that the Board of Peace reversed its disarmament terms on 3 August, and the Middle East Institute (November) calls the West Bank economy a crisis. [5][6]
context_md: Hamas-led militants attacked Israel on 7 October 2023, killing about 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages, according to AP. [7] Gaza's health ministry, part of the Hamas-led government, counts 74,618 Palestinians killed since then as of 4 November 2026. [8] A US-brokered ceasefire took effect on 10 October 2025, and Israel recovered the last hostage's remains on 26 January 2026. [9] The ceasefire plan put Gaza's transition under the Board of Peace, but its second phase, covering Hamas disarmament, Israeli withdrawal, an international force and reconstruction, has stalled. [10] In the West Bank, the EU counts more than 750,000 Israeli settlers in 147 settlements and a growing number of outposts, about 15 percent of the West Bank population by its count. [11] The Palestinian Authority under Mahmoud Abbas, 90, administers parts of the West Bank, and national parliamentary elections were last held in 2006. [12]

sections.title: A ceasefire with 1,658 deaths under it and a new Israeli ground push
sections.body_md:
The ceasefire that took effect on 10 October 2025 has not stopped the killing. Gaza's health ministry says 1,658 Palestinians have been killed and about 6,000 wounded since it began, and the Israeli military says five of its soldiers have died in the same period. [13] AP reported seven Israeli soldiers killed in late September, so the two counts of Israeli deaths do not match, and neither report explains the gap. [7] The ministry does not separate civilians from fighters. [7]

On 18 November Israeli tanks moved into central Gaza west of the Yellow Line, the boundary of the area Israel controls, which Reuters puts at roughly two-thirds of the Strip. Some residents told Reuters it was the first ground raid since the ceasefire. [3] The Israeli military said it was acting against Hamas infrastructure and reserves the freedom to act against immediate threats. [13] Defence Minister Israel Katz says Israel will not withdraw until Hamas is dismantled, and has said Israel could seize more territory and add it to a permanent security perimeter. [13]

Hamas calls the raid a flagrant violation of the ceasefire. Its official Basem Naim dismissed the Board of Peace's report to the UN as "pure disinformation". [13] Israel says Hamas is regrouping and rearming. [3] Israeli security assessments cited by Ynet say Hamas runs checkpoints and collects levies of up to about 50 percent in some cases on aid goods. [2] Gaza's Government Media Office counts 5,989 Israeli ceasefire violations since the truce began, 753 of them in October. [14]

lenses.local: Al-Quds repeats the health ministry's daily toll and its attribution of 1,602 deaths since the ceasefire to Israeli violations, and Ynet reports Southern Command reinforcing the Yellow Line. In November 2025 the IDF spokesman told the Times of Israel that Hamas "tests us daily". [1][2][15]
lenses.international: Reuters and Al Jazeera report the raid and the competing Israeli and Hamas accounts of it. [3][13]
lenses.scholar: Crisis Group counted more than 1,200 people killed by Israeli strikes since the truce as of August and says Israeli forces have pushed beyond the Yellow Line. [5]

sections.title: Phase two is stalled: a July disarmament roadmap, a reversal, and a committee kept out of Gaza
sections.body_md:
The ceasefire plan places Gaza's transition under the US-backed Board of Peace, which oversees a Palestinian technocratic body, the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), led by Ali Shaath from Cairo. Al Jazeera reports that Israel has not let it enter Gaza and has not said why. No international stabilisation force has deployed. Six countries (Indonesia, Morocco, Kazakhstan, Albania, Kosovo and Uganda) have committed personnel to a planned force of 20,000 soldiers and 12,000 police. [10]

On 30 July mediators from Egypt, Qatar, Turkey and the US announced a roadmap for phased Hamas disarmament, with weapons held by a Palestinian committee and Israeli withdrawals in step with verification. Hamas negotiator Ghazi Hamad said Hamas would take no step unless Israel met its withdrawal obligations, and Israel did not publicly accept the plan. [16] Crisis Group says Israel rejected it and that the Board of Peace then reversed its terms on 3 August, insisting on full disarmament first. [5]

In a report to the Security Council on 17 November, the Board said Israel and Hamas had both fallen far short of their commitments. It said Israel had blocked the technocratic administration, had not decided the conditions for training and deploying Palestinian police, and had restricted supplies. [17] The Board also accused Hamas of continued armed activity and of taxing goods entering Gaza. [13] Netanyahu and Katz have said there will be no reconstruction before Hamas is disarmed. [2] PSR's August poll found 72 percent of Palestinians opposed to disarmament before a full Israeli withdrawal, and 24 percent trusting the Board of Peace. [18]

lenses.local: PSR's August poll of 1,270 Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank found 32 percent trust in the NCAG and 24 percent in the Board of Peace. [18]
lenses.international: Al Jazeera, drawing partly on AP, reports the Board's warning that the ceasefire could collapse and that a stalled truce "cannot be sustained indefinitely". [17]
lenses.scholar: Crisis Group argues that the Board's decisions are concentrated in a small US team and that it has deferred to Israel, and Lancaster University's Simon Mabon told Al Jazeera the Board has failed. [5][10]

sections.title: Famine is over by the IPC's count, but all of Gaza is in crisis and winter is coming
sections.body_md:
The IPC said on 23 July that no part of Gaza is in famine, after it had declared famine in parts of the Strip in August 2025. [4] Its special snapshot classifies the whole Strip in Phase 3 (crisis). It counts 1,239,657 people (59 percent) in Phase 3 or worse between 16 April and 30 June and projects 1,412,421 (67 percent) from July to December, with none in Phase 5. It calls the gains fragile and says aid coverage fell from 2.13 million people in November 2025 to 1.49 million in May 2026. [19]

Israel disputes the premise of the hunger reporting. COGAT, the Israeli military body that oversees aid, rejected the IPC's findings and said its own data show truck entries nearly three times the required amount by World Food Programme benchmarks. Israel says the problem is distribution inside Hamas-controlled areas, and COGAT acknowledged that commercial goods make up about half of what has entered since the ceasefire. [4] OCHA's 29 October report lists 651 UN and partner trucks for entry, a 16 percent weekly drop, and says flour and fresh produce prices reportedly rose more than 70 percent after commercial imports stalled over disputed fees. [20] Counts of daily trucks differ: Al Jazeera cites the IPC for about 227 aid trucks a day against 600 planned, and Ynet reports about 600 a day. [10][2]

OCHA reports 1.98 million people (94 percent) needing shelter help and flood risk at displacement sites ahead of winter. [8][20] IOM says about 100,000 tents are waiting to enter. [13] The EU and UN damage and needs assessment released on 20 April puts recovery and reconstruction at more than $71 billion over ten years, including $26.3 billion in the first 18 months, and counts 371,888 housing units destroyed or damaged. [21]

lenses.local: Ynet carries Israeli security assessments that Hamas taxes aid, and Al-Quds repeats a claim, attributed to unnamed reports, that about 90 percent of civilian infrastructure is destroyed. [2][1]
lenses.international: AP reports the IPC's findings alongside COGAT's rejection of them. [4]
lenses.scholar: The IPC rates its evidence as high for all areas analysed, and says about 17 percent of the population near the Yellow Line and Netzarim Corridor was left out of its nutrition survey, so conditions there may be worse. [19]

sections.title: Counting the dead: a ministry figure of 74,618, a survey that supports it, and no independent press inside Gaza
sections.body_md:
The casualty figure most cited comes from Gaza's Ministry of Health: 74,618 killed and 175,920 injured as of 4 November 2026. [8] AP notes that the ministry is part of the Hamas-led government and does not distinguish civilians from fighters, that UN agencies and international organisations generally regard its records as reliable, and that the ministry says women and children are about half the toll. [7] Israel has long questioned the figures, but an Israeli army official told journalists in January that the army accepted about 70,000 deaths. [22]

A household survey published in The Lancet Global Health, led by Michael Spagat of Royal Holloway, University of London, estimated 75,200 violent deaths between 7 October 2023 and 5 January 2025, against 49,090 reported by the ministry for the same period. The authors called the ministry's records reliable and, if anything, conservative. [22] On the Israeli side, AP gives about 1,200 killed on 7 October and 251 hostages taken, and the Israeli military's website counts 474 soldiers killed since the ground operation began. [7][8]

Counts of journalists killed differ. The Palestinian Journalists Syndicate counts 262 media workers killed as of 30 June, while CPJ documented 209 killed by Israel as of 25 June and removed 20 names from its database during a review, eight of them after evidence that they were Hamas or Islamic Jihad combatants. [8][23] CPJ says Israel has refused access to Gaza for international correspondents, so researchers outside cannot verify cases in person. [23]

lenses.local: Al-Quds relays the ministry's daily toll without independent verification. [1]
lenses.international: AP states the ministry's limits and the UN's view of its reliability in its toll reports. [7]
lenses.scholar: Spagat's survey is the main check on the ministry's counts found for this draft. [22]

sections.title: West Bank: record settler attacks, a Hebron lockdown, and Israeli and UN accounts that diverge
sections.body_md:
OCHA recorded 397 settler attacks between 1 and 26 October, the highest monthly number since its documentation began in 2006. In the week of 20 to 26 October it logged 62 attacks causing casualties or damage across 49 communities, 38 of them linked to the olive harvest. [20] For 2025 OCHA counted 1,828 settler attacks, also a record, with nine Palestinians killed. [11] HRW reports that attacks increasingly reach Area B and occur with soldiers present or standing by. [24] Amnesty says the pressure on Bedouin and herding communities amounts to ethnic cleansing, and cites OCHA data on 117 communities displaced fully or partly from January 2023 to April 2026. [25] B'Tselem counts 75 communities displaced by its own measure and at least 1,107 Palestinians killed by Israel in the West Bank between October 2023 and September 2026. [26]

Israeli authorities reject or qualify these accounts. The Israeli military told Amnesty that its forces respond to settler attacks, detain suspects until police arrive and investigate cases where troops may have failed to intervene. [25] Katz told Channel 7 in July that the government had approved 104 new settlements since 2022, HRW reports. [24] On 8 February Israel's security cabinet approved measures expanding Israeli control over land, including in Areas A and B, and Secretary-General Guterres warned that this erodes prospects for a two-state solution. [27]

After two Israeli soldiers were killed in an attack on 23 October, Israel locked down Hebron. The city's mayor says 2,200 people were forced from their homes, Katz said about 2,000, and the municipality told OCHA about 3,000, a figure OCHA says it is still verifying. Katz said the displaced would not return until the Hamas issues in Hebron were resolved, and the Palestinian Authority called the operation collective punishment. [28][20] The EU counts 63,311 settlement housing units advanced in 2025, a record, and final approval in August 2025 for 3,401 units in the E1 area, which it says would bisect the West Bank. [11]

lenses.local: Hebron's mayor, the activist Issa Amro and Wafa supply the Palestinian accounts in Al Jazeera's Hebron report, and Katz supplies the Israeli one. [28]
lenses.international: OCHA, HRW and Amnesty document the attacks and displacement, and the EU report counts the settlement approvals. [20][24][25][11]
lenses.scholar: MEI's November memo counts more than 1,000 Palestinians and at least 41 Israelis killed in the West Bank since October 2023. [6]

sections.title: The Palestinian Authority: elections pushed to September 2027 while Israel controls its revenue
sections.body_md:
On 10 October Abbas decreed that the Legislative Council election set for 28 November 2026 will instead be held together with a presidential election on 11 September 2027. The PLO Executive Committee said conditions in East Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza are unsuitable and that Israel has not allowed election materials or international observers into Gaza. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar accused Abbas of fooling the international community. The Palestinian National Initiative's Mustafa Barghouti said everything is concentrated in the hands of the executive authority. Abbas has ruled by decree since his term should have ended in 2009. [12]

PSR's August poll (1,270 interviews, margin of error 3.5 percent) found 79 percent of Palestinians want Abbas to resign, and support for Hamas and Fatah at 24 percent each. In a hypothetical presidential race, 54 percent chose Marwan Barghouti and 14 percent Abbas. [18]

The treasury runs on money Israel collects. MEI says Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, now in a caretaker government, is withholding clearance revenues (the memo gives no figure), capping shekel repatriation and granting only short bank-indemnity extensions to the end of 2026, and that about 100,000 work permits were revoked after October 2023. [6] In 2025 the Times of Israel reported that clearance revenues were about 65 percent of the PA budget, that Israel deducts sums tied to payments to prisoners' families, and that Prime Minister Mohammad Mustafa said the economy had contracted by 30 percent in a year, a PA claim. Smotrich's office did not respond to the paper. [29] B'Tselem puts West Bank unemployment above 31 percent in 2024. [26]

lenses.local: PSR's polling and Wafa, as relayed by Al Jazeera, carry the Palestinian view, and Palestinian officials describe the postponement as forced by Israeli restrictions. [18][12]
lenses.international: Al Jazeera reports the postponement together with Israeli criticism of it. [12]
lenses.scholar: MEI calls the West Bank economy a crisis driven by Israeli policy and PA fiscal weaknesses, and recommends transparency measures for the PA and predictable clearance transfers from Israel. [6]

sections.title: Courts and inquiries: the ICJ case runs to 2029, and Israel rejects the UN commission's genocide finding
sections.body_md:
In South Africa's case at the International Court of Justice, Israel filed its Counter-Memorial in March 2026 and objected to the court's jurisdiction. The timetable gives South Africa until 22 November 2027 to reply and Israel until 22 May 2029 to file a rejoinder, and no hearing date is set. South Africa's presidency says self-defence is no defence to genocide and that the court's provisional measures remain binding. [30]

On 26 October the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry, chaired by Srinivasan Muralidhar, reported that Israeli authorities committed crimes against humanity in the West Bank, including extermination, torture, rape and persecution, and that Israeli forces continued genocidal acts in Gaza after the ceasefire. It also said the Palestinian Authority targeted people who voiced dissent. The commission does not speak for the UN as a whole. [31] Israel's mission in Geneva called the report part of a misinformation campaign, urged states to reject it and demanded the commission's dissolution. [31] Amnesty calls on other states to impose targeted sanctions on Netanyahu, Ben-Gvir, Katz, Smotrich and Orit Strock. [25]

lenses.local: B'Tselem, an Israeli rights group, says Israel is pursuing an elimination project against Palestinian life in the West Bank and urges states to end complicity. [26]
lenses.international: Al Jazeera and the Mail & Guardian report the commission's findings and the ICJ timetable, and Al Jazeera carries Israel's rejection. [31][30]
lenses.scholar: Legal scholarship was not reviewed in this draft beyond the commission's findings and the court's published steps.

sections.title: Israel's 27 October election produced no majority and left Netanyahu as caretaker
sections.body_md:
Israel voted on 27 October, its first election since the 7 October 2023 attack. With counting complete, Netanyahu's bloc won 53 of 120 seats, the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot 48 and Arab-led parties 19, so no side reached the 61 needed. Results were due to be certified the following week. [32] Eisenkot has pledged not to partner with Arab-led parties, yet Al Jazeera's correspondent Nour Odeh says the opposition cannot form a government without them. [32]

Likud alleged, without substantiation, that Arab-led parties stole the election. Noam Sohlberg, head of the Central Elections Committee, said he had received serious suspicions of foreign interference, could not verify them and asked the Shin Bet to investigate. [32] Netanyahu remains in a caretaker role, according to MEI. [6] Hamas says his caretaker government is escalating in Gaza to deflect from domestic crises, a claim the sources read do not answer. [13] Days before the vote Netanyahu declined to say whether he would dismantle the Palestinian Authority and said a big surprise awaited it. [28]

lenses.local: Ynet reports that Southern Command is preparing for a possible order to disarm Hamas by force, and that Katz says the army is ready to finish the job if ordered. [2]
lenses.international: Al Jazeera reports the seat counts, the coalition arithmetic and the unsubstantiated fraud claims. [32]
lenses.scholar: Analyst Xavier Abu Eid told Al Jazeera that cooperation between the opposition and Arab-led parties looks unlikely. [32]

factchecks.by: Widely repeated since the IPC's August 2025 famine declaration
factchecks.evidence: The IPC's 23 July 2026 snapshot finds no area in Phase 5 and no famine classification, with the whole Strip in Phase 3 (crisis) and acute malnutrition at acceptable levels, though it calls the gains fragile and projects 1.41 million people in Phase 3 or worse through December. Israel denied that a man-made famine ever existed, and COGAT rejected the IPC's findings.

gaps: Palestinian local sourcing is thin: Wafa, Maan and Gaza-based outlets were not read directly, and Al-Quds was read for one day's toll. Local sources are otherwise Israeli outlets (Ynet, The Times of Israel), and Haaretz was not read.

Israeli government primary documents (prime minister's office, foreign ministry, COGAT) were not read directly; Israeli positions come through Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera, Ynet and the Times of Israel. Hamas statements likewise come only through third-party reports.
Al Jazeera is flagged state_affiliated (Qatari funding) and supplies many items; wires, Israeli outlets, UN agencies and NGOs are used to balance it, and several of its facts rest on one outlet.
No independent journalists can enter Gaza, so casualty, aid and violation figures (health ministry, Government Media Office, IDF, COGAT) could not be independently checked.

Counts of Israeli soldiers killed since the ceasefire differ (AP 7 in September, Reuters and Al Jazeera 5 in November) and are unexplained. Aid-truck counts (about 227 versus about 600 a day) and the number of Hebron displaced (2,000, 2,200, 3,000) also differ, and definitions were not checked.
Counts of displaced West Bank communities differ by source and date (HRW 107, Amnesty 117 from OCHA data to April 2026, B'Tselem 75 by its own measure) and were not reconciled.
Amnesty and Crisis Group reports were read in part (first 100,000 characters), and the B'Tselem report and the Lancet survey were read only through Al Jazeera's coverage.

Not covered: East Jerusalem (evictions, Al-Aqsa access), UNRWA's status, Israeli NGO registration rules, detainees and prison conditions, Gaza health system detail, and Israeli coalition talks after 29 October.

Podcast and film entries point to a transcript page and an interview page; episode length and release platforms were not shown. Book years come from a review date, a prize listing and a list page, not from publisher pages.

name: Palestine

scores.coverage_basis: Reuters, AP and Al Jazeera file on Gaza and the West Bank most days, and OCHA, Crisis Group, HRW and Amnesty publish on weekly to monthly cycles [3][4][20]. Israel has refused access to Gaza for international correspondents, so first-hand reporting depends on local journalists and agencies [23]. West Bank incidents draw less wire attention than Gaza, although OCHA tracks them weekly [20].

severity.basis: Gaza's health ministry counts 1,658 killed since the ceasefire and Israeli tanks re-entered central Gaza on 18 November, while OCHA recorded the most settler attacks in a month since 2006 [13][20].
The IPC places all of Gaza in Phase 3 with 1.41 million projected in Phase 3 or worse, and OCHA reports 1.98 million people needing shelter help ahead of winter [19][8].

Palestinian elections slipped to September 2027, the UN commission reports crimes against humanity in the West Bank, which Israel rejects, and international journalists cannot enter Gaza [12][31][23].
The EU and UN put recovery needs above $71 billion and report an economy contracted by 84 percent, and MEI says the West Bank economy is in crisis [21][6].
The Board of Peace warns of collapse and Israel has begun a ground push, but the IPC finds famine over and acute malnutrition at acceptable levels [17][19].

parts.basis: The US backs the Board of Peace and a stabilisation force planned under US Central Command, while Egypt, Qatar and Turkey mediate [10][16].
The sums at stake are reconstruction aid, with needs put above $71 billion over a decade [21].
Crisis Group warns Israel could resume full-scale war, and MEI warns West Bank instability could push Palestinians toward Jordan [5][6].
The 7 October attack took 251 hostages and the EU and UN count 1.9 million displaced in Gaza, while MEI says at least six US citizens have been killed in the West Bank since early 2024 [7][21][6].
The ICJ case runs to 2029, the UN commission reports genocidal acts and crimes against humanity, and Crisis Group says the Board of Peace has expanded beyond its UN mandate [30][31][5].

summary: Palestine's weight beyond its borders comes from law and precedent, great-power diplomacy and the risk of wider war, more than from trade [30][31][10]. The Board of Peace model, the ICJ case and the commission of inquiry each test how international bodies act on an occupation and a war, and each is contested by Israel [31][5].
gi.up: A collapse of the ceasefire into full-scale war, a Palestinian Authority fiscal collapse, or a large flight of West Bank residents toward Jordan.
gi.down: Verified phased disarmament with Israeli withdrawal and a technocratic committee governing inside Gaza.
